title: Operating System Structure
body:
How the [[Operating System|OS]] is carved into pieces, and which of those pieces run
privileged. It is a [[Coupling and Cohesion]] question about a program that happens to be a
kernel, which is why [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]] points here: the OS is the
standard worked example of layering, and of what layering costs.

The constraint that makes it interesting: crossing from user code into the kernel is not a
function call. It needs a [[System Call]], which means a trap, a privilege change into
[[Supervisor State]], and a [[Context Switching|context switch]]. [[Kernel]] owns that
hardware boundary; this note is about what you put on each side of it.

## The designs

| Structure | Idea | Good | Bad |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monolithic | one big privileged program; anything can call anything | fast, no boundary crossings | high coupling, one bad driver panics the machine |
| Layered | each layer only uses the one below | clean dependencies, easy to reason about | a request crosses every layer, and layers are hard to order honestly |
| Microkernel | kernel does IPC and scheduling only; drivers and file systems are user processes | a crashed driver is a crashed process, not a dead machine | every service call is now [[Message Passing]] |
| Modular | monolithic core plus loadable modules | most of the speed, some of the isolation | modules still run privileged |

Linux is the last row: monolithic in the sense that it all runs in kernel space, modular in
that drivers load and unload at runtime.

## The trade, in one line

**Every boundary you add buys isolation and costs a crossing.** A microkernel's file system
is a separate process, so a bug in it cannot corrupt the scheduler; but reading a
[[File]] now means IPC to that process instead of a function call. That is
[[Coupling and Cohesion]] with a measurable price tag attached, which is what makes the OS
a better example of it than most software.

## What runs where

- **Kernel space**: scheduling ([[CPU Scheduling]]), [[Virtual Memory]] and the page
  tables, interrupt handling, the [[Control Block|control blocks]]. Privileged, and in a
  monolithic kernel the drivers and [[File Systems]] are here too.
- **User space**: everything else, including the [[Shell]]. Reaches the kernel only through
  [[System Call|system calls]].
